simple.meaning: אִכָּר (ʼikkâr) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a farmer.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 7 times across 2 Chronicles, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Joel, Amos, beginning at 2 Chronicles 26:10. Its contexts include flock, land, mountain, wilderness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אִכָּר (H406).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אִכָּר (ʼikkâr) / H406 is traced through 2 Chronicles 26:10, Isaiah 61:5, Jeremiah 14:4, Jeremiah 31:24 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H406. ikkar אִכָּר noun masculine Joel 1:11 ploughman, husband-man (Arabic , Aramaic , אִיבָּרָא , compare Mishna) ׳א singular absolute Jer 51:23 (+ וְצִמְדּוֺ ) Amos 5:16 ; plural אִכָּרִים Jer 14:4 ; 31:24 (|| בָעֵדֶר וְנָָֽסְעוּ ) 2Chr 26:10 (|| כֹּרְמִים ) Joel 1:11 (|| id. ,), אִכָּרֵיכֶם Isa 61:5 (|| id. ) אַכְשָׁף see כשׁף . I. אַל (= , Arabic article, preserved perhaps in following words derived by Hebrews from (or through) Arabic-speaking tribes; compare English algebra, Alhambra, alkali, alcohol, alcove , etc.)
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to dig ;

occurrences.englishText: He built towers in the wilderness, and dug out many cisterns, for he had much livestock; in the lowland also, and in the plain. He had farmers and vineyard keepers in the mountains and in the fruitful fields, for he loved farming.
Strangers will stand and feed your flocks.
Because of the ground which is cracked,
Judah and all its cities will dwell therein together, the farmers, and those who go about with flocks.
With you I will break in pieces
Therefore Yahweh, the God of Armies, the Lord, says:
